php2shell 
 
 CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 — PHP Pre-Auth RCE Exploit & Detection Toolkit 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Exploits · Detection · Lab · ITW Tracker · Writeup · Week 1 Report 
 

---

Five independent RCE chains exploiting PHP's session.upload progress and the Zend engine's OOM bailout. 14 years of vulnerable code — PHP 5.4.0 (2012) through 8.5.11. Pre-auth. No application vulnerability required for some chains.

Impacts 78% of all websites — including WordPress (43%), Joomla, Drupal, Laravel, Magento, and every default PHP installation.

 Author: Qi Deng     Writeup: Substack     Week 1 Report: Substack     Date: 2026-10-21

 CVE Details

 CVE GHSA CVSS Description 
 ----- ------ ------ ------------- 
 CVE-2026-109618 GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w 9.2 OOM → longjmp() leaves Zend engine state invalid → RCE 
 CVE-2026-109619 GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp 9.2 Stale global state across FPM worker requests → UAF → RCE 

 Patch: Commit 3584a98 — 300 files changed across the Zend engine.

 Attack Chains

 Chain Vector Pre-auth Conditions SAPI 
 ------- -------- :--------: ------------ ------ 
 A Session injection + LFI Yes App has any LFI sink All 
 B var destroy UAF → handler overwrite No App calls unserialize() All 
 C Handler mismatch → destruct Yes Two dirs with different serialize handler FPM 
 D OOM corruption → stale EG() Yes None — any endpoint mod php 
 E FPM session OOM → stale BG() Yes Producer: any session start() endpoint; Consumer: any endpoint FPM 

Chain D is the most critical: zero-dependency pre-auth RCE against any Apache mod php installation.

Chain E is nearly as broad on FPM: the producer needs any endpoint that calls session start() (near-universal — WordPress, Laravel, Joomla, Drupal all do), and the consumer can be any PHP endpoint — the rfc1867 upload progress handler runs during SAPI startup before application code. Verified: nosession.php (no session start() in code) triggers 502 crash when consuming stale BG(unserialize) state.

 Exploits

Three RCE exploits (Chains A, B, C) are included in exploit/ :

 File Chain What It Does 
 ------ ------- ------------- 
 chain a session lfi.py A Injects PHP code via upload filename → LFI includes session file → RCE 
 chain b uaf rce.php B var destroy UAF → discovers zif system via EG() → overwrites var dump handler via /proc/self/mem → RCE 
 chain c mismatch rce.py C Pollutes FPM worker PS(serializer) → injects serialized object via filename → destruct fires on decode failure → RCE 

Chains D and E exploits are available to paid subscribers.

 

 Detection Rules

Pre-built IDS / WAF / SIEM rules in detection/ :

 File Format Signatures 
 ------ -------- ----------- 
 php2shell.rules Suricata / Snort 13 rules — request, response, and recon 
 php2shell.yaml Sigma 5 rules — web logs, process creation, file events 
 modsecurity.conf ModSecurity v2/v3 7 rules — drop-in for Apache/Nginx 
 php2shell.lua OpenResty Lua Lightweight reverse proxy module 

 Fastest mitigation: block PHP SESSION UPLOAD PROGRESS in multipart POST bodies. Near-zero legitimate use, covers the primary attack vector for both CVEs.

 Quick Start

 

 Repository Structure

 

 Mitigation

 

 The only complete fix is patching PHP to 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12+. The OOM corruption (Chain D) is in the Zend engine core — no INI setting fixes it.

For legacy / EOL environments (PHP 5.4–8.1) where upstream provides no official security updates, community-maintained backports with deployment automation and verification tooling are available at Anton-Barinov/php2shell-patches.

 Exploitation in the Wild

 CISA KEV listed (2026-10-26)     Confirmed RCE on honeypot (2026-10-24)     Millions of attempts within 24h

Full analysis: PHP2Shell One Week Later (Substack)     Live tracker with IOCs: docs/EXPLOITATION.md 

Highlights:
- ASLR bypass PoC leaked addresses via Set-Cookie — works on x86 64 with production config, no debugger needed
- Potassium (Mirai fork) delivered via php2shell — ChaCha20-encrypted config, 20 DDoS commands, reverse shell
- Downstream pre-auth RCE confirmed on WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Magento, Roundcube, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, Laravel, Symfony, MediaWiki, WooCommerce, Shopware, WHMCS

 Downstream Impact

Wiz has demonstrated pre-auth RCE on stock container images:

 Platform Vulnerable Notes 
 ---------- :----------: ------- 
 WordPress Yes Core doesn't use PHP sessions, but WooCommerce and many plugins do 
 Joomla Yes Uses native PHP sessions by default 
 Drupal Yes Uses native PHP sessions by default 
 Magento Yes Vulnerable even in maintenance mode 
 Laravel Yes PendingBroadcast is a known destruct gadget 
 Roundcube Yes Webmail — credential exposure risk 
 phpMyAdmin Yes Direct database access 
 Nextcloud Yes File storage system 
 Symfony Yes Framework-level exposure 
 MediaWiki Yes Wiki platform 
 WooCommerce Yes WordPress plugin; payment data at risk 
 Shopware Yes E-commerce platform 
 WHMCS Yes Hosting control panel 

See docs/EXPLOITATION.md for full details, IOCs, and attacker tooling.

 References

- PHP Security Advisory
- GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w — CVE-2026-109618
- GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp — CVE-2026-109619
- Patch commit 3584a98 — 300 files, Zend engine + extensions
- Cloudflare WAF coverage
- Sansec analysis — PHPSESSID heap leak discovery
- Wiz downstream impact
- Corelight detection — Zeek + Suricata community rules
- Wiz exploitation analysis — Honeypot data, remediation stats
- ELLIO sensor data — First-seen timeline, payload observations
- VulnCheck exploit — Production-config ASLR bypass
- Nokia Deepfield Potassium — Mirai-variant botnet analysis
- Community EOL Backports (PHP 5.4–8.1) — fleet-validated patches, deploy tooling & verification suite

 Disclaimer

This repository is for authorized security testing and educational purposes only . Exploit code for Chains D and E (zero-dependency RCE) is available to paid subscribers of the writeup.

install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/ikow/php2shell-poc.git && cd php2shell-poc

# Start the lab (PHP-FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php)
cd lab && docker compose up -d

# Verify each chain
python3 ../poc/verify_session_injection.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080
python3 ../poc/verify_handler_mismatch.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080
python3 ../poc/verify_oom_trigger.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081
python3 ../poc/verify_fpm_stale_state.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080

# Run an exploit
python3 ../exploit/chain_a_session_lfi.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 --command 'id'
